title: Tanzanian Coconut Milk Rice
community: Swahili coast — coconut milk rice at its simplest and best
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Tanzanian Wali wa Tui — long-grain rice cooked entirely in fresh coconut milk. Even simpler than Wali wa Nazi, this version forgoes all additions — pure rice, pure coconut milk, pure Zanzibar. Every grain is infused with coconut.
longDesc: Wali wa Tui is the purest expression of the Swahili coast's love for coconut — rice cooked in nothing but fresh coconut milk. No spices, no additions, no embellishment. The coconut milk does everything: it flavours, enriches, and colours the rice a beautiful creamy white.
ingredients: 3 cups long-grain rice — washed and soaked 20 minutes
steps: Combine coconut milk, water, and salt. Bring to a boil.
Drain soaked rice. Add to boiling coconut milk.
Stir once. Bring back to a boil.
Cover tightly. Reduce to lowest heat.
Cook 18—20 minutes without lifting the lid.
Rest 10 minutes. Fluff gently with a fork.
chefTips: Fresh coconut milk only — this dish reveals the difference immediately.
The rice will have a slightly cream colour and a rich fragrance.
commonMistakes: Using canned coconut milk without adjustment.
cookingScience: See TZA002 for coconut rice cooking science.
culturalNote: Wali wa Tui is the rice that makes everything else taste better — served alongside the coast's finest fish curries and meat stews, its gentle coconut fragrance is the thread that ties the whole coastal meal together.
